facts.raw_span: abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus 2 days earlier and migrated to the right lower quadrant
no prior abdominal surgeries or systemic disease
denied anorexia, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, weight loss, night sweats, diarrhea, or constipation
afebrile

blood pressure was 130/95 mm Hg
voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant
minimal tenderness elsewhere
white-cell count of 15,600/mL
hemoglobin of 14.2 g/dL
plain abdominal X-rays demonstrated several air–fluid levels without free air under the diaphragm
ultrasound assessment was interpreted as compatible with plastron appendicitis

concepts.why: The patient's abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, voluntary guarding, elevated white-cell count, and imaging findings are consistent with acute appendicitis.
The ultrasound assessment compatible with plastron appendicitis, along with the patient's symptoms and laboratory findings, supports this diagnosis.
The presence of a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen on computed tomography and the patient's abdominal pain could be indicative of intussusception.
The patient's symptoms, including abdominal pain and voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant, along with the elevated white-cell count, could be consistent with cecal diverticulitis.
The patient's abdominal pain, voluntary guarding, and elevated white-cell count could be indicative of typhlitis, although the absence of neutropenia makes this diagnosis less likely.
The patient's symptoms, including abdominal pain and voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant, along with the elevated white-cell count, could be consistent with Meckel's diverticulitis.
The patient's abdominal pain and voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant could be indicative of epiploic appendagitis.
The patient's abdominal pain and voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant could be consistent with omental infarction.
The presence of air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays and the patient's abdominal pain could be indicative of perforated visculitis.
The patient's abdominal pain and the presence of a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen on computed tomography could be consistent with cecal volvulus.

rationales.F01: The patient's abdominal pain migrating to the right lower quadrant is highly suggestive of appendicitis.
rationales.F07: Voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant is a common finding in appendicitis.
rationales.F09: An elevated white-cell count is a common finding in appendicitis and other inflammatory conditions.
rationales.F11: The presence of air-fluid levels on plain abdominal X-rays is consistent with an obstructive process, such as appendicitis or intussusception.
rationales.F12: The ultrasound assessment compatible with plastron appendicitis strongly supports this diagnosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The ultrasound assessment was interpreted as compatible with plastron appendicitis, and the patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with this diagnosis, with no strong contradictions.
